first.rationale: Targeted pricing directly addresses the competitive loss among price-sensitive SMBs, but its evidence needs verification for incrementality, retention, and qualified-revenue durability. Signup simplification is the strongest alternative because it may address both declining onboarding completion and activation; its downstream revenue linkage also requires confirmation. Run only a guarded, segmented pricing test if the source record supports durable qualified value rather than discount-driven volume.

final.rationale: Run SMB signup/onboarding simplification. The verified record shows +9% activation and +4% qualified revenue, directly addressing both declining onboarding completion and activation, with only a -1% 30-day-retention signal to guardrail. Reject promotional pricing: its verified +18% qualified-revenue lift came with -12% 30-day retention and explicitly failed the sustainable-growth criterion. Use retention and qualified revenue as decision guardrails and keep the rollout SMB-scoped because the result was not replicated elsewhere.
